title: Baldwin effect or hiding effect? Lifetime learning and the evolution of innate foraging
question: Does reward-modulated lifetime learning speed up the evolution of innate foraging ability (Baldwin effect / genetic assimilation), or does it shield genotypes from selection so innate ability evolves less (hiding effect)?
background: Theory predicts both directions (Hinton & Nowlan 1987; Mayley 1997; Paenke, Sendhoff & Kawecki 2007). We measure innate foraging by assaying evolved genomes alone, with learning switched off, so only the inherited wiring is tested. A no-mutation control checks whether mutation plus selection improves innate foraging at all.

hypotheses.statement: Baldwin: learning populations evolve HIGHER innate foraging
Hiding: learning populations evolve LOWER innate foraging
Mutation + selection improves innate foraging over selection among founder genomes alone
